feed.title: Google Cloud: Model Armor
feed.subtitle: Changelog for Google Cloud product: Model Armor

entry.content:
Clarification: August 5, 2026 release note for Melbourne and Seoul

In Melbourne (australia-southeast2) and Seoul (asia-northeast3), only the Sensitive Data Protection filter is supported when data residency is enforced. To use other Model Armor features in these regions, disable data residency enforcement in the template.

For information about available Model Armor features for each region, see Supported features by region.
entry.summary: For Melbourne and Seoul, only the Sensitive Data Protection filter is supported with data residency enforced. Other Model Armor features require disabling data residency enforcement in the template.
entry.title: Feature: Data Residency Clarification for Melbourne and Seoul

entry.content:
Filter version v3 will be promoted to the Stable alias on or before September 25, 2026. On the same date, filter versions v1 and v2 transition to Legacy status and retire on November 29, 2026.

If your templates use the Stable alias, they will automatically upgrade to v3 when it is promoted. If your templates use explicit version numbers (v1 or v2), migrate them to v3 or the Stable alias before November 29, 2026.

For more information, see Set the filter version for a template.
entry.summary: Filter version `v3` will be promoted to the `Stable` alias on or before September 25, 2026. On the same date, filter versions `v1` and `v2` will transition to `Legacy` status and retire on November 29, 2026. If your templates use the `Stable` alias, they will automatically upgrade to `v3`. If you are using explicit version numbers, migrate them to `v3` or the `Stable` alias before November 29, 2026.
entry.title: Feature: Filter version v3 promoted to Stable

entry.content:
You can disable data residency enforcement for in-use and in-transit data in Model Armor templates. Disabling data residency enforcement allows cross-jurisdictional routing to enable Model Armor features that are otherwise unavailable in limited-support regions. Data at rest remains compliant with data residency requirements.

For more information, see Set data residency compliance and Data residency and endpoints.
entry.summary: You can now disable data residency enforcement for in-use and in-transit data in Model Armor templates. This allows for cross-jurisdictional routing, enabling features that might otherwise be unavailable in limited-support regions, while data at rest remains compliant with residency requirements.
entry.title: Feature: Disable data residency enforcement for in-use data

entry.content:
Model Armor supports screening prompts and responses up to 65,536 tokens (262,144 characters) for prompt injection and jailbreak detection, responsible AI, and child sexual abuse material (CSAM) filters. Model Armor scans only the first 256 URLs found in prompts and responses.

For more information, see Token system limits.
entry.summary: Model Armor now screens prompts and responses up to 65,536 tokens for various safety filters, including prompt injection, jailbreak detection, responsible AI, and CSAM. It scans the first 256 URLs within these prompts and responses to ensure comprehensive protection.
entry.title: Feature: Enhanced prompt and response screening

entry.content: The prompt injection and jailbreak detection filter for the Mumbai (asia-south1) and Singapore (asia-southeast1) regions is upgraded to improve detection accuracy and reduce the rate of false positives.
entry.summary: The prompt injection and jailbreak detection filter in the Mumbai and Singapore regions has been upgraded. This enhancement aims to improve detection accuracy and minimize false positives, ensuring safer AI interactions.
entry.title: Change: Improved AI safety filter in Asia

entry.content: Model Armor is integrated with Google Agentspace to provide greater insights and enhanced security of your agent interactions by default. For more information, see Integration with Google Agentspace.
entry.summary: Model Armor now integrates with Google Agentspace, offering enhanced security and insights into agent interactions.
entry.title: Feature: Model Armor and Agentspace Integration

entry.content: Model Armor integration with Google Kubernetes Engine is available in General Availability.
entry.summary: Model Armor integration with Google Kubernetes Engine is now generally available.
entry.title: Feature: Model Armor now on GKE

entry.content: The Model Armor monitoring dashboard provides a centralized view to track interactions and violations within your projects. This feature is available in Preview. For more information, see View the monitoring dashboard.
entry.summary: Introducing the Model Armor monitoring dashboard, a new feature providing a centralized view to track interactions and violations within your projects.
entry.title: Feature: Model Armor Monitoring Dashboard

entry.content: Model Armor supports the asia-southeast1 location. For information about supported locations, see Locations for the Model Armor API.
entry.title: Changed: Model Armor supports new location

entry.content: You can use Terraform to manage Model Armor floor settings and templates. This helps reduce manual overhead with Model Armor deployments. For more information, see Terraform resources for Security Command Center.
entry.summary: Manage Model Armor settings with Terraform.
entry.title: Feature: Terraform for Model Armor
